transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I guess I'm here because... well, I've been having a little trouble keeping up with some of my work lately. I'm a high school teacher, which I really love, but... I don't know if this is normal, so please tell me if I'm just overthinking it. 

When I sit down with a stack of essays or a curriculum document, I really do fully intend to just focus and get through it. But I've noticed that, maybe ten minutes in, I'll realize I've just been staring at the exact same page. My mind just kind of wanders off to three other things, and I barely even take in what's right in front of me. I mean, I know everyone gets a little distracted sometimes, right? But it's been happening enough that I thought I should probably ask someone about it. Does that make sense?
How long have you been experiencing these difficulties with focusing?

Um, well... I guess it's been noticeably worse for about 11 months now? Give or take. The school changed up our curriculum calendar around then, and they also added these new after-school planning meetings. 

Which, I mean, I really shouldn't complain, it's just part of the job, right? I want to be a team player. But ever since they added those extra things to my plate, it just feels like my brain kind of... hits a wall. I feel like I should be able to handle it just fine, like all the other teachers do. I really hope I don't sound like I'm just making excuses for falling behind. Is it normal for a schedule change like that to throw someone off so much?
Looking back to your childhood or school years, did you ever struggle with focus, daydreaming, or staying organized?

Um... well, I guess if I really think back... yeah, maybe a little bit? I mean, I was a good kid, I promise I wasn't causing trouble or anything! But, um, my parents did have to stay on top of me quite a bit. 

Like, even in primary school, I remember my report cards always having those little notes... you know, the ones that said I was "bright but careless," or that I wouldn't finish my work unless someone was right there keeping an eye on me. Which I always felt so bad about! And my parents would always find these crumpled-up worksheets at the bottom of my backpack that I had completely forgotten to turn in. I guess I was just a little scatterbrained? I mean, a lot of kids are like that though, right? It's probably just normal kid stuff... I hope that's the kind of thing you were asking about?

Um... well, yes, I suppose it does bleed over a little bit. But I really don't want to make it sound like my whole life is a mess, because it's not! I try really hard to keep things together. 

But, um... at home, my wife has sort of... taken over doing the bills and keeping track of our schedule and reminders. Which is so incredibly sweet of her, she's wonderful. I think she just realized she couldn't really count on me to remember those things, no matter how much I wanted to. I always felt terrible when I'd forget a due date or double-book us. I guess it's just easier for her to handle it now. Is it okay that she does that? I hope it doesn't make me sound like a terrible husband.

And, um, I guess I should probably mention—though I'm really embarrassed about this—at work, it's gotten a little bit... noticeable. The missed follow-through, I mean. My department chair actually put me on a, um, a support plan recently. Which sounds really bad, I know! But they framed it as just a way to help me get back on track, and I'm really, really trying to do everything they ask. I just want to do a good job, you know? I hope that doesn't make you think I'm a bad teacher... I really do care about my students.
